symbols.name: model1D
symbols.summary: This function can be used to obtain a physical model in 1 dimension. Takes a force input signal for each point and outputs the state of each point.

params.name: points
params.description: size of the mesh in points

params.name: R
params.description: neighbourhood radius, indicates how many side points are needed (i.e. if R=1 the mesh depends on one point on the left and one on the right)

params.name: T
params.description: time coefficient, indicates how much steps back in time are needed (i. e. if T=1 the maximum delay needed for a neighbour state is 1 sample)

params.name: scheme
params.description: coefficients scheme

symbols.name: model2D
symbols.summary: This function can be used to obtain a physical model in 2 dimension. Takes a force input signal for each point and outputs the state of each point. IMPORTANT: 2D models with more than 30x20 points might crash the c++ compiler. 2D models need to be compiled with the command line compiler, the online one presents some issues.

params.name: pointsX
params.description: horizontal size of the mesh in points

params.name: pointsY
params.description: vertical size of the mesh in points

params.name: R
params.description: neighbourhood radius, indicates how many side points are needed (i.e. if R=1 the mesh depends on one point on the left and one on the right)

params.name: T
params.description: time coefficient, indicates how much steps back in time are needed (i. e. if T=1 the maximum delay needed for a neighbour state is 1 sample)

params.name: scheme
params.description: coefficients scheme

symbols.name: stairsInterp1D
symbols.summary: Stairs interpolator in 1 dimension. Takes a number of signals and outputs the same number of signals, where each one is multiplied by zero except the one specified by the argument. This can vary at run time (i.e. a slider), but must be an integer.

params.name: points
params.description: total number of points in the mesh

params.name: point
params.description: number of the desired nonzero signal

symbols.name: stairsInterp2D
symbols.summary: Stairs interpolator in 2 dimensions. Similar to the 1-D version.

params.name: pointsX
params.description: total number of points in the X direction

params.name: pointsY
params.description: total number of points in the Y direction

params.name: pointX
params.description: horizontal index of the desired nonzero signal

params.name: pointY
params.description: vertical index of the desired nonzero signal

symbols.name: linInterp1D
symbols.summary: Linear interpolator in 1 dimension. Takes a number of signals and outputs the same number of signals, where each one is multiplied by zero except two signals around a floating point index. This is essentially a Faust implementation of the $J(x_i)$ operator, not scaled by the spatial step. (see Stefan Bilbao's book, Numerical Sound Synthesis). The index can vary at run time.

params.name: points
params.description: total number of points in the mesh

params.name: point
params.description: floating point index

symbols.name: linInterp2D
symbols.summary: Linear interpolator in 2 dimensions. Similar to the 1 D version.

params.name: pointsX

params.name: pointsY

params.name: pointX
params.description: horizontal float index

params.name: pointY
params.description: vertical float index

symbols.name: schemePoint
symbols.summary: This function calculates the next state for each mesh point, in order to form a scheme, several of these blocks need to be stacked in parallel. This function takes in input, in order, the force, the coefficient matrices and the neighbours’ signals and outputs the next point state.

params.name: R
params.description: neighbourhood radius

params.name: T
params.description: time coefficient

params.name: D
params.description: scheme spatial dimensions (i.e. 1 if 1-D, 2 if 2-D)

symbols.name: hammer
symbols.summary: Implementation of a nonlinear collision model. The hammer is essentially a finite difference scheme of a linear damped oscillator, which is coupled with the mesh through the collision model (see Stefan Bilbao's book, Numerical Sound Synthesis).

params.name: coeff
params.description: output force scaling coefficient

params.name: omega0Sqr
params.description: squared angular frequency of the hammer oscillator

params.name: sigma0
params.description: damping coefficient of the hammer oscillator

params.name: kH
params.description: hammer stiffness coefficient

params.name: alpha
params.description: nonlinearity parameter

params.name: k
params.description: time sampling step (the same as for the mesh)

params.name: offset
params.description: distance between the string and the hammer at rest in meters

params.name: fIn
params.description: hammer excitation signal (i.e. a button)

symbols.name: bow
symbols.summary: Implementation of a nonlinear friction based interaction model that induces Helmholtz motion. (see Stefan Bilbao's book, Numerical Sound Synthesis).

params.name: coeff
params.description: output force scaling coefficient

params.name: alpha
params.description: nonlinearity parameter

params.name: k
params.description: time sampling step (the same as for the mesh)

params.name: vb
params.description: bow velocity [m/s]
